chunks: A group informed me, from Abū Muḥammad Hārūn ibn Mūsā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan; and Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from his uncle Yaʿqūb al-Aḥmar, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
Regarding a menstruating woman: may she dye herself with henna? He said: “The Shayṭān is not feared for her at that time.”

key_terms.الشَّيْطَانُ: Satan, mentioned here in relation to fear or harm
key_terms.الْحَائِضِ: a woman in the state of menstruation
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman under discussion in the ruling
key_terms.تَخْتَضِبُ: she applies dye, such as henna
key_terms.عِنْدَ ذَلِكَ: at that time or in that circumstance

ai.seo_question: Can a menstruating woman apply henna according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the case of a menstruating woman and asks whether she may apply dye such as henna. The Imam عليه السلام replies in a concise legal form, indicating that there is no fear from Shayṭān for her in that state, which conveys permissibility in context.
